transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood), Maya (VelvetSearch Head of Search), Connor (VelvetSearch Lead ML), Priya (CTO)

Summary: quick hosted API walkthrough focusing on embeddings + reranking for site search relevance. Customer interested in accuracy improvements and predictable latency/cost for 200 RPS peak. Discussed security and POC next steps.

00:00 Avery: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, we set aside an hour to run through the hosted embeddings + rerank demo, and then def take q's. is that still good on time?
00:06 Maya: yes thanks, excited to see how this fits into our search stack, we currently use elastic with a hybrid vector layer.
00:12 Samir: cool, i'll share my screen, quick context questions first maya, conner: what's your current flow for embeddings and rerank? are you doing bi-encoder then cross-encoder re-rank?
00:22 Connor: yeah, roughly. we index bi-encoder vectors in our vector db (pinecone today), then use a cross encoder for top-10 re-rank. latency is...hit or miss at scale, and cost for cross-encoder is expensive.
00:31 Priya: our SLO is p95 < 200ms for search results but we're open to relaxed tail when re-rank happens but want predictable cost.
00:40 Samir: thanks - thats helpful. our hosted api supports embeddings endpoint and a rerank endpoint pattern; we do recommend doing vector search first then calling the rerank for top-k to save cost. i'll demo an end-to-end flow using your sample data shape.
01:05 Samir (screen): so here is the Redwood Console, the hosted embeddings endpoint returns a 1536-d or 4096-d vector depending on model - we have curated models that balance latency vs accuracy. note that the model catalog lists performance profiles, example: 'redwood-search-base' yields faster vectors, 'redwood-cross-large' used for rerank. slight typo in the auto labels sometimes shows Redwoood on the console but not relevant.
01:40 Maya: quick q - do you store vectors for hosted or do we store them?
01:44 Avery: good question - with hosted api you push embeddings to your vector store; we return vectors and you index them. Hosted also supports a managed embeddings index add-on but that's an extra.
01:58 Connor: and for rerank, is that remote call to a cross-encoder? how do you handle tokenization and prompt consistency?
02:05 Samir: rerank endpoint is a simple POST where you pass candidate docs and the query; by default we use our cross-encoder model and you can configure temperature and prompt templates. tokenizer mismatches can happen across libs, we include a bundle of tokenizer helpers in the SDK.
02:30 Samir: demo time - i'm going to run a sample top-k flow: 1) call /v1/embeddings -> index vectors in your store; 2) run vector similarity locally to get top-20; 3) call /v1/rerank with top-20 to get re-ordered list.
02:55 [screen action, a few seconds of typing]
03:10 Samir: example request body, passing query, candidates (id + text), we show score and normalized score. response returns scores + optional explanation metadata. note: sometimes the transcripter mis-renders the explanation key as 'explainashun' in our logs.
03:45 Maya: looks good, what latencies are typical for rerank for top-10 on hosted?
03:50 Samir: depends on model and size. for our small-medium cross encoders p95 is ~80-120ms in hosted environment; large models can be 250-400ms. we recommend trimming candidates to top-20 and using a medium cross encoder for strict tail SLOs.
04:12 Connor: that's promising. what about cost ballpark for 1M queries per month with 10 candidates on rerank?
04:20 Avery: rough calc - embeddings cost + rerank compute. we'll send a pricing sheet, but rough estimate is $Xk/month for medium model; dedicated reserved capacity can reduce unit cost if you commit.
04:32 Priya: we'd consider dedicated later if cost pushes too high, but first want to validate hosted with a POC. security wise we need SOC2, SSO, and KMS for keys.
04:45 Avery: totally - we have SOC 2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS integrations; we'll share the security pack. private/VPC options also available if you need audit boundaries.
05:00 Maya: for the POC, we will share a subset of our queries and dataset (100k docs), want to run hosted benchmarks for latency and top-n MAP.
05:08 Samir: perfect - for the benchmark we have a spreadsheet template, we'll use your queries and a fixed sampling. i'll prepare a recommended rerank config (candidate size, model selection, batching).
05:22 [brief cross talk while Samir navigates to example notebook]
05:40 Samir: also want to show console traces - this is the per-route latency breakdown, token-level cost, and request traces. here's an example trace for a rerank call showing embedding call, vector fetch, rerank call. helps debug where tail latency comes from.
06:10 Maya: nice, do you have automatic batching?
06:15 Samir: yes, the runtime does continuous batching where possible; batching policy is tunable per-route. for hosted we expose recommended batch sizes in the console.
06:30 Connor: what about caching? we have frequent queries that could reuse prefix KV.
06:35 Samir: we support prefix caching and optional KV cache for session-based reranks; that can dramatically reduce tokens for chat-like flows. for search rerank, caching top results is common.
07:00 Priya: any compliance concerns storing queries in your logs? we need retention controls and audit.
07:06 Avery: logs are adjustable - retention policies, redaction, and you can enable audit export to your SIEM. for Private deployments we can keep all logs in your VPC.
07:30 Maya: competitors - we've talked to pinecone and elastic, what are Redwood differentiators?
07:35 Avery: main diff is unified inference + observability for both embeddings and rerank, plus smart routing and cost controls. we expose per-token cost and suggestions via Optimize to lower unit cost.
07:52 Connor: sounds good. small nit - integration complexity? our infra uses Kubernetes on GKE and we want to keep CI/CD simple.
07:58 Samir: hosted is a couple API calls plus SDK; for Private we'll provide helm charts and an operator. Dedicated is an intermediate with reserved GPU pools.
08:20 [demo continues: Samir shows SDK snippet and small notebook run]
10:00 Samir: running a sample rerank now, uploading sample candidate set... results back in ~95ms for medium model, normalized scores and explanation tokens shown.
10:18 Maya: output looks cleaner than our current cross-encoder, interesting how it handles long docs.
10:25 Samir: note we do truncation and chunking heuristics; you can supply chunk metadata and we reassemble.
10:40 Connor: curious about model versioning and rollouts - can we pin versions and do canary?
10:45 Samir: yes, per-route model pinning and canary rollouts supported. console shows rollout % and metrics.
11:00 Priya: for the POC timeline we want results in two weeks. is that feasible?
11:04 Avery: yes - 1 week to run benchmarks + 1 week to evaluate. we'll target kickoff May 10.
11:12 [customer asks deeper technical questions - Samir addresses batching knobs, gRPC endpoints, concurrency settings; some technical terms garbled by transcription]
20:00 Samir: also want to mention quantization options for dedicated/private which reduce model size and cost - we can recommend quant profiles based on your latency targets.
20:15 Connor: good to know. our docs are long, i'll share schema and sample repo.
25:30 [mid-call recap]
25:35 Avery: recap: we'll send pricing and security docs, Samir will prepare benchmark plan and config, Connor to share data and queries, we schedule POC kickoff for 2027-05-10. any other questions?
25:48 Maya: no, thanks. small ask - can you include an example curl and node snippet for embeddings+rerank in the follow-up?
25:55 Samir: yes will include in email.
26:10 [minor audio glitch for ~10s causing a couple words to drop]
26:25 Priya: one more Q, SLA for hosted?
26:28 Avery: hosted has best-effort but we offer SLA for Dedicated/reserved customers; we can discuss for enterprise.
26:40 Maya: ok great.
30:00 [closing logistics, confirm next meeting]
31:00 Avery: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and calendar invite for kickoff.
31:10 Connor: thanks all.

References shared during call: https://redwood.ai/docs/hosted-embeddings (deck), https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-pack (security pack), https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/velvet-template (benchmark sheet)

End of transcript.
